rule.title: ERC-1967 proxy/implementation exposes upgradeTo without a strong upgrade guard (bytecode evidence)

intent.attack_thesis: Runtime bytecode embeds the ERC-1967 implementation slot constant AND exposes an upgradeTo / upgradeToAndCall selector while no strong upgrade-authorization framework (Ownable2Step, AccessControl, TimelockController, two-step upgrade acceptance) is detected. The contract also performs delegatecall, so a successful impl-pointer swap pivots execution into attacker code on the next proxy call. This is the bytecode-evidence variant of proxy.unprotected_implementation_upgrade and fires regardless of whether the storage modeler resolves the impl slot.

reporting.title_template: Implementation contract exposes upgradeTo without a strong upgrade guard (bytecode evidence)
reporting.summary: Bytecode contains the ERC-1967 implementation slot constant and an upgradeTo / upgradeToAndCall selector, the contract performs delegatecall, but no strong upgrade-authorization framework was identified.
reporting.user_summary: The contract appears to be the logic side of an ERC-1967 proxy and exposes an upgrade entrypoint without a strong upgrade guard. An attacker who can reach the upgrade function may be able to swap the proxy's implementation to malicious code, which the proxy will then delegatecall into.
reporting.technical_summary: Bytecode-level evidence: the runtime PUSH32-embeds the EIP-1967 implementation slot constant (0x360894a1...382bbc) and contains the upgradeTo(address) selector (0x3659cfe6) or upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes) selector (0x4f1ef286). None of the strong upgrade-guard frameworks (Ownable2Step / AccessControl / TimelockController / two-step acceptance) are detected. This is the bytecode-pattern variant of proxy.unprotected_implementation_upgrade and fires on tag-set match without depending on the storage modeler resolving the impl slot.
reporting.exploit_narrative: The attacker locates the upgradeTo entrypoint, calls it with an attacker-controlled implementation contract, and immediately triggers a proxy delegatecall that lands in the malicious implementation. The proxy's execution authority is lost.
exploit_preconditions: no strong upgrade-authorization framework gates the call
remediation_hints: wrap upgrade entrypoints in OpenZeppelin Ownable2Step / AccessControl / TimelockController
adopt a two-step upgrade acceptance pattern
emit upgrade events and enforce implementation allowlists

steps.action: call upgradeTo passing attacker-controlled implementation address
steps.expected_state: EIP-1967 implementation slot updated to malicious contract

witness_goal.success_condition: implementation slot contains attacker-controlled address; subsequent proxy calls delegate to malicious contract
